title: Letters Re: Audit of the Financial and Operating Practices of 12 Bronx Community Boards
plain_title: Leave warnings as Bronx community board audit is called off
what_they_audited: This is a set of closure letters, not a full audit report. The Comptroller's office told Bronx community boards that a planned audit of the financial and operating practices of the borough's 12 boards was terminated, and it flagged excess annual leave balances for the district managers of Boards 2, 10 and 12.
background: Recent changes to the New York City Charter allow the Comptroller to treat all community boards as a single combined agency, so auditing one board's operations in a four-year cycle now fulfills the mandate. Before the change, the office had to audit all 59 community boards every four years.

findings.plain: The planned audit of the 12 Bronx community boards was terminated because charter changes let the Comptroller satisfy the audit mandate by examining a single board in each four-year cycle.
findings.quote: This decision was made based on recent changes to the New York City Charter which allows the Comptroller to treat all Community Boards as a single combined agency.

findings.plain: The district manager of Bronx Community Board 2 had banked 841.75 hours of annual leave as of November 25, 2024, which is 561.75 hours (80.3 days) over the two-year maximum for managers. Auditors estimated the payout on separation at $46,098.62 with a waiver to carry over the excess and $17,455.99 without one.
findings.quote: an annual leave balance of 841.75 hours, as of November 25, 2024

findings.plain: The district manager of Bronx Community Board 10 had 496.5 hours of annual leave, 174.5 hours (24.9 days) over the limit, with an estimated separation payout of $24,405.37 with a waiver and $16,851.04 without one.
findings.quote: an annual leave balance of 496.5 hours, as of November 25, 2024

findings.plain: The district manager of Bronx Community Board 12 had 688.75 hours of annual leave, 338.75 hours (48.4 days) over the limit, with an estimated payout of $51,154.67 with a waiver and $30,208.81 without one. That larger figure equals 32% of the manager's salary and 20% of the board's fiscal year 2025 personal services budget.
findings.quote: an annual leave balance of 688.75 hours, as of November 25, 2024

findings.plain: Under the city personnel order, managers may only bank two years of annual leave unless the agency head grants a waiver; without one, excess leave converts to sick leave that pays out at one-third the balance. Either way, unmanaged accruals can strain a board's small budget.
findings.quote: a Community Board’s budget and fiscal health can be crippled if leave accruals are not effectively managed

recommendations: Encourage the district manager to use annual leave and shrink the accrued balance to limit the lump sum payment owed when the manager leaves city service.
Limit authorizations to carry over excess annual leave where practicable.
Establish protocols for monitoring future leave accruals and ensure compliance with the personnel order's leave regulations.
